title: Assidat zgougou (Aleppo pine seed cream; substitute pine nuts)

ingredients.name: Aleppo pine seeds (zgougou), or raw pine nuts, ground to a fine powder
chopped nuts, pine nuts and sugared almonds, to decorate

steps: Whisk the ground pine seeds and flour with the water in a saucepan until smooth, then add the sugar.
Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, for 15 to 20 minutes until the mixture thickens to a smooth, dark cream. Stir in the orange blossom water and pour into small bowls or glasses.
For the white topping, whisk the milk, cornflour, 2 tablespoons of sugar and the egg yolk in a pan and cook gently, stirring, until thick and smooth.
Cool both layers slightly, then spoon the white custard over the dark base.
Decorate with chopped nuts, pine nuts and sugared almonds, and chill before serving.

title: Bambalouni (Tunisian fried doughnuts)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the egg and warm milk and knead into a soft, sticky dough, 8 to 10 minutes.
Cover and let it rise for about 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oil to about 175 C (350 F). With oiled hands, pinch off egg-sized pieces of dough, flatten them into thick discs and, if you like, press a hole in the middle.
Fry the doughnuts a few at a time for 2 to 3 minutes per side until puffed and golden brown.
Drain on paper towels, then roll in sugar or drizzle with warm honey while still hot. Eat fresh.

title: Fricasse (Tunisian fried tuna-filled rolls)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the warm water and olive oil and knead for 10 minutes into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 8 to 10 balls, shape each into an oval roll about 12 cm long and rest on a floured tray for 20 minutes.
Heat the frying oil to about 170 C (340 F) and fry the rolls in batches for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until puffed and deep golden. Drain on paper towels.
Mix the tuna with the mashed potato, olives, capers, preserved lemon and harissa into a rough filling.
Split each warm roll open lengthways, spread harissa inside if you like, fill with the tuna mixture and slices of egg.
Serve straight away while the rolls are still warm and crisp.

title: Harissa (Tunisian hot chilli paste)

ingredients.name: dried red chillies (such as guajillo or New Mexico), stems and seeds removed
olive oil, plus extra to cover

steps: Soak the dried chillies in hot water for 20 to 30 minutes until soft, then drain and squeeze out the water.
Put the chillies, garlic, caraway, coriander, cumin, salt and lemon juice in a food processor, or pound in a mortar.
Add the olive oil gradually and blend into a thick, rough paste.
Spoon into a clean jar, level the surface and cover with a thin layer of olive oil.
Keep in the fridge for up to 2 weeks, topping the oil layer up after each use. Serve with bread, in stews, with eggs or as a table condiment.

title: Homemade merguez (spicy lamb sausages with harissa)

ingredients.name: minced lamb, with some fat (about 20 per cent)
set of sausage casings (optional; the mixture can also be shaped by hand)

steps: Mix the minced lamb with the harissa, paprika, cumin, fennel, coriander, garlic and salt, and knead well for a couple of minutes until it is sticky.
Chill the mixture for at least 2 hours so the flavours mingle.
Either stuff the mixture into prepared sausage casings and twist into 10 cm links, or shape into thick finger-shaped sausages with wet hands.
Pan-fry or grill over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through with no pink in the middle.
Serve in bread with grilled peppers, or with couscous and a green salad.

title: Kamounia (Tunisian beef and liver cumin stew)

ingredients.name: beef stew meat, cut into cubes
beef or lamb liver, cut into cubes
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Heat the olive oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef well in batches. Remove and set aside.
Fry the onions in the same pot until soft and golden, then add the garlic, cumin, paprika and tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Return the beef, add the hot water, salt and pepper, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low heat for 1 to 1.5 hours until the beef is tender.
Add the liver and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes only, until just cooked, so it stays tender.
Check the seasoning, stir in plenty of parsley and serve with rice or bread.

title: Makroudh (Tunisian semolina and date diamonds)

ingredients.name: warm water, plus a splash of orange blossom water
soft pitted dates (Deglet Nour if possible)

steps: Rub the oil into the semolina with the salt until it holds together when squeezed, then add the warm water a little at a time and knead briefly into a smooth dough. Rest for 1 hour.
Mash the dates with the cinnamon and a little orange blossom water into a thick paste.
Roll the dough into logs about 3 cm wide, press a groove down the middle of each, lay a thin rope of date paste inside and pinch the dough closed over it.
Gently flatten the logs a little, then cut each diagonally into diamonds about 4 cm wide.
Fry the diamonds in medium-hot oil for 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until golden. Drain.
Warm the honey with the water until runny and soak the hot makroudh in it for a minute, then lift out onto a rack. Cool before serving.

title: Mechouia salad (Tunisian grilled pepper and tomato salad)

ingredients.name: green or red bell peppers (or a mix with 2 hot green chillies)
black olives and salt, to taste

steps: Grill or roast the peppers, tomatoes, onion and garlic cloves over a flame or under a very hot grill, turning, until the skins are blackened and the flesh is soft; the garlic will take less time.
Put the peppers in a covered bowl for 10 minutes, then peel off the skins and remove the seeds. Peel the tomatoes, onion and garlic.
Chop everything finely (traditionally it is crushed to a coarse paste with a knife or a mortar), keeping some texture.
Stir in the caraway, olive oil, lemon juice and salt, and let it sit for 15 minutes to blend.
Spread it on a plate, top with flaked tuna, egg quarters and olives, and drizzle with a little more olive oil.
Serve cool or at room temperature with bread, as a starter or a side dish.

title: Mesfouf (Tunisian sweet steamed couscous with dried fruit)
steps: Put the couscous in a bowl, sprinkle with a pinch of salt and about 100 ml of warm water, and rub it with your fingers to separate the grains.
Steam it in a sieve or couscoussier over simmering water, covered, for 15 minutes, then tip it out, sprinkle with a little more water and fluff it up.
Steam again for 15 minutes until the grains are tender.
Toss the hot couscous with the butter, sugar, orange blossom water and most of the raisins, dates and almonds.
Mound on a plate and decorate with the remaining dried fruit and nuts.
Serve warm with hot milk poured over, or cold with yogurt.

title: Mloukhia (Tunisian dark green mulukhiyah beef stew)

ingredients.name: beef stew meat (or lamb), cut into chunks
dried mulukhiyah (jute leaf) powder, or 300 g of dried leaves
salt and black pepper to taste; bread or rice to serve

steps: Brown the beef in a few tablespoons of the oil in a heavy pot, then add the garlic, coriander, tomato paste and bay leaves and stir for a minute.
Add enough hot water to cover the meat, season with salt and pepper and simmer, covered, for about 1 hour until the beef is nearly tender.
Mix the mulukhiyah powder with the remaining oil into a paste, then stir it into the pot with the rest of the hot water.
Cook very slowly on low heat for 2 to 3 hours, stirring regularly and scraping the bottom, until the stew is thick, glossy, nearly black-green and the oil rises to the surface.
Taste for salt and serve with bread, or with rice or boiled potatoes.

title: Tabil (Tunisian coriander and caraway spice mix)

ingredients.name: dried chilli flakes, or to taste

steps: Toast the coriander and caraway seeds in a dry pan over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until they smell fragrant, shaking the pan.
Let the seeds cool completely, then grind them to a fine powder in a spice grinder or mortar.
Mix in the chilli flakes and garlic powder.
Store in an airtight jar for up to 3 months.
Use it to season stews, soups, meatballs, couscous or roasted vegetables, starting with 1 teaspoon per 4 servings.

title: Tunisian chorba (lamb, tomato and orzo soup with mint)

ingredients.name: ground caraway or tabil spice mix
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot and fry the lamb and onion for 8 minutes until the lamb is browned and the onion soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, harissa and caraway and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the water or stock, salt and pepper, bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 45 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Add the chickpeas and orzo and cook for 10 minutes until the pasta is tender.
Stir in the dried mint, taste for seasoning and serve hot with lemon wedges and bread.

title: Tunisian couscous with lamb and vegetables

ingredients.name: pumpkin or butternut squash, cut into chunks
salt and black pepper to taste

steps: Heat the oil in the bottom of a large pot (a couscoussier if you have one) and brown the lamb, then add the onions and cook until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste, harissa, caraway, coriander, salt and pepper, add the water and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots and turnips and cook for 15 minutes, then the pumpkin and chickpeas and cook for another 15 to 20 minutes until all vegetables and the lamb are tender.

Meanwhile, put the couscous in a bowl, sprinkle with a little salted water and rub through with oiled fingers to break up lumps. Steam it in a sieve over the simmering stew, covered, for 20 minutes, or soak it in an equal volume of hot water for 10 minutes, then fluff.
Tip the couscous into a large dish, work in the butter and a ladle of stew broth and fluff with a fork.
Mound the couscous on a platter, top with lamb and vegetables and serve with a bowl of broth and extra harissa.
